children: , the world's largest contract chipmaker, anchored a new Kaohsiung industrial park designed to tighten the link between advanced-packaging development, testing and workforce training. The U.S.-listed shares gained approximately 0.6% to $447.86, extending investors' focus beyond wafer fabrication and deeper into the packaging bottleneck shaping the AI-chip boom.

TSMC plans to occupy two buildings at the site, including a laboratory and training center, with operations targeted for the fourth quarter of 2029. Industrial facilities will cover 53.6 hectares of the 88.7-hectare park, roughly 60% of the total area, giving equipment and materials suppliers space to test technologies closer to TSMC's qualification process. That matters because packaging is becoming a bigger part of the performance race as increasingly complex AI accelerators require tighter integration of chips, memory and substrates.

The valuation picture adds another angle. At $447.86, TSMC trades 23.32% above its GF Value estimate of $363.17, showing how much future growth investors are already pricing into the shares. The Kaohsiung project could shorten the path from supplier innovation to production approval, but it should not be mistaken for an immediate capacity surge: TSMC disclosed no investment figure, output target or customer commitment. For now, the story is about faster qualification and a stronger packaging ecosystemnot instant volume.

title: TSMC Gains as Packaging Moves Closer to Its Suppliers
